Guidance & outlook: As far as the Q1 FY27 performance, coming to our quarterly performance, our revenue for Q1 FY27 grew by 9.1% year-on-year to ₹19.4 crores.

Working on the balance hubs is on track and we remain confident of achieving the full FY27 target of 10 new hubs, followed by eight new centres in FY28 and one in FY29 in line with the phase roll-out we had shared at the time of listing.

In addition, our board has approved an estimated project cost of up to ₹15 crores for the Gaudium Women Hospital at Lucknow, which will be incurred progressively over the setup and commissioning phase, with the commercialization expected in FY28-FY29.
Growth & demand: Growth was driven primarily by higher patient volumes at our major hubs, sustained traction in advanced IVF protocols, and a steady contribution from international patients.
One is even at a lower base of ₹17.8 crores around in Q1 FY26, we grew just 9% Y-o-Y.

So that is why we are confident that eventually at the end of the year, we will be able to meet our projected growth which is also again proven by our historical growth year-on-year which has been around 30% whereas the industry CAGR is around 10% to 12%.
Margins & costs: Reported EBITDA and PAT for the quarter stood at ₹2.4 crores and ₹1.8 crores respectively, moderating on a year-on-year basis.
Reported EBITDA margin stood at 12.5% for the quarter versus 29% in Q1 FY26.

Excluding these expansion related one-off costs, EBITDA would have been approximately ₹5.35 crores with an EBITDA margin of approximately 27.63%, broadly in line with our steady state operating profile.
Capex & expansion: I am happy this is our first full quarter as a publicly listed company, and I'm pleased to share that it has been a quarter of steady, disciplined execution, one that reflects both the strength of our clinical foundation and the momentum of our expansion roadmap.
The quarter saw developments on the expansion side that I believe are particularly Gaudium IVF and Women Health Limited August 14, 2026 important.

Capex phasing, on the capex front, for FY27, we had earlier guided a capex of approximately ₹25 crores for the 10 new hubs at an estimated average cost of ₹2.5 crores per hub, funded primarily through IPO proceeds and internal accruals.
Balance sheet & cash: Our clinician-led DNA, our SOP driven asset light hub and spoke model refined over 17 years, our AI powered signature lab framework, our debt-light balance sheet post IPO, and a category that is just beginning its growth curve in India.
Our balance sheet continues to remain robust and debt-light post the IPO, giving us the flexibility to fund our expansion plan with adequate financial cushion.
Cash and bank balances as on 30th June stood at ₹8.12 crores against the borrowings of ₹6.74 crores and our consolidated debt-to-equity ratio remains comfortably at approximately 0.04 times.
Risks & challenges: Add to this delayed parenthood, rising awareness, a steadily reducing stigma, and a very meaningful medical tourism opportunity where the cost of an IVF cycle in India is roughly 1/5th of what it is in the United States Gaudium IVF and Women Health Limited August 14, 2026 Gaudium is well placed to be one of the principal beneficiaries of this shift and you w…

The early clinical benefits of our AI embryology tools which we formally integrated in partnership with IVF 2.0 are beginning to reflect in embryo selection consistency and in better sperm selection with the use of both these software.
Now innovation, what it does is, it makes us stand out from the competition, as you very rightly asked that there is so much competition, you know, how do we stand out.
